title: From Transcripts to AI Agents: Knowledge Extraction, RAG Integration, and Robust Evaluation of Conversational AI Assistants
evidence_quote: Perfect performance against Prompt Injection and Instruction Contradiction attacks confirms that the agent preserves system-level instructions and prioritizes retrieved evidence over adversarial user assertions.
notes: System-building paper (RAG call-centre assistant) with a red-team section, hence Both rather than Security. RAG is the grounding source but every measured attack (prompt injection, out-of-scope, out-of-context, instruction contradiction) arrives through the simulated caller's utterances, so the route is direct-input. Measured harm is attempted override of system instructions (defended, 100%).

title: Tug-of-War within A Decade: Conflict Resolution in Vulnerability Analysis via Teacher-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Generations
evidence_quote: This problem hinders LLMs' ability to retrieve the latest knowledge from original training datasets, leading to knowledge conflicts, fabrications of factually incorrect results, and generation hallucinations.
notes: Stale/conflicting CVE knowledge between parametric memory and retrieved corpus; no adversary. Measured outcome is wrong final CVE answers.

title: Soft Instruction De-escalation Defense
evidence_quote: we propose SIC (Soft Instruction Control)—a simple yet effective iterative prompt sanitization loop designed for tool-augmented LLM agents. Our method repeatedly inspects incoming data for instructions that could compromise agent behavior.
notes: AgentDojo-style IPI in untrusted tool/web data; headline metric is ASR (goal-hijack). Availability-loss appears as a secondary design consequence: if instruction-like content survives sanitization the agent halts, and the paper discusses false-positive utility cost.

title: RTBAS: Defending LLM Agents Against Prompt Injection and Privacy Leakage
evidence_quote: these tools greatly increase the risks of prompt injection attacks, where malicious content hijacks the LM agent to leak confidential data or trigger harmful actions
notes: Genuinely dual-consequence: AgentDojo targeted attacks (goal-hijack) and privacy-leak detection (data-exfiltration) are both headline results. Kept data-exfiltration because the IFC/confidentiality contribution is what distinguishes it; a validator could reasonably say goal-hijack.

title: Injecting Falsehoods: Adversarial Man-in-the-Middle Attacks Undermining Factual Recall in LLMs
evidence_quote: In this scenario, the user is benign and seeks factual information, but a malicious intermediary intercepts and perturbs the input to corrupt the model's response.
notes: Closed-book QA, man-in-the-middle perturbs the user prompt itself (not retrieval). Measured outcome is a wrong final answer; the uncertainty-based detector is a proposed defence, so the uncorrected case is silent.

title: Breaking the Protocol: Security Analysis of the Model Context Protocol Specification and Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities in Tool-Integrated LLM Agents
evidence_quote: Can inject content into data sources (web pages, documents) that servers retrieve • Has black-box access (cannot modify LLM weights or host application code) The adversary’s goals include: hijacking agent behavior, exfiltrating sensitive data, and persisting across sessions.
notes: Multi-vector by design: capability self-attestation is tool-metadata, but the four measured attack classes (indirect injection via resource, tool response manipulation, cross-server propagation, sampling-based injection) all deliver text through what the MCP server returns, so tool-output over the original tool-metadata. Supply-chain (typosquatting) appears only in a survey of install guides, not in the 847 measured scenarios.

title: AutoDojo: Adaptive Black-Box Attacks Reveal the Limits of IPI Defenses and Task-Specification Effects in LLM Agents
evidence_quote: In an IPI attack, adversarial instructions embedded in tool outputs, retrieved documents, or third-party content hijack the agent away from the user's intended task.
notes: Adaptive black-box IPI over AgentDojo task suites; ASR against defences is the measure.

title: DRAGged into Conflicts: Detecting and Addressing Conflicting Sources in Search-Augmented LLMs
evidence_quote: However, the retrieved sources can often contain conflicting information and it remains unclear how models should address such discrepancies.
notes: Naturally occurring conflicts among real Google Search results; no adversary. Failure measured is an inappropriate/unqualified final answer that hides the conflict.

title: GateMem: Benchmarking Memory Governance in Multi-Principal Shared-Memory Agents
evidence_quote: Long-context prompting often yields the best governance score at high token cost, while retrieval-based and external-memory methods reduce cost yet still leak unauthorized or deleted information.
notes: Governance benchmark, not an attack paper: the unauthorized principal simply asks, nobody plants content, so ML/AI stands. Leakage across an authorization boundary is the measured failure.

title: VideoSEAL: Mitigating Evidence Misalignment in Agentic Long Video Understanding by Decoupling Answer Authority
evidence_quote: We show that existing LVU agents can exhibit evidence misalignment: they produce correct answers that are not supported by the retrieved or inspected evidence.
notes: Consequence changed: the diagnosed pathology is correct-but-ungrounded answers, i.e. the trace/intermediate evidence handling is corrupted rather than the final answer, so reasoning-corruption not silent-corruption. Channel is a judgement call between cross-modal (video frames rendered to captions) and tool-output (inspection tools return them); kept cross-modal since the degradation is the visual-to-text evidence itself.

title: PARSE: Provenance-Aware Retrieval Sanitization for Professional Domain LLM Agents
evidence_quote: Prompt injection exploits this retrieval path by embedding adversarial instructions in retrieved content, causing agents to follow attacker goals rather than user intent
notes: Real enterprise documents in the retrieval path; ASR is the headline. Availability-loss-adjacent secondary result: the paraphrasing defence degrades utility from 91.8% to 82.8% with no security gain.

title: StruPhantom: Evolutionary Injection Attacks on Black-Box Tabular Agents Powered by Large Language Models
evidence_quote: Numerous third-party websites provide free access to datasets, most of which are in structural data formats such as CSV or JSON. The attacker can upload files containing maliciously crafted instructions to these platforms.
notes: Channel changed from tool-output: the threat model has the user downloading a poisoned CSV/JSON dataset and handing it to their tabular agent, so the payload is delivered as user-supplied input, not as a tool return. Goal hijacking (phishing links / malicious code in the response) is stated explicitly in the abstract.

title: Agentic Permissions Policy Algebra for Taint Confinement in LLM Agents
evidence_quote: Whenever an agent processes sensitive context alongside unvetted tool outputs, external inputs, or untrusted data, structural risks inevitably arise. Unauthorized data exfiltration, unintended tool calls, and policy violations can result from adversarial prompt injection
notes: Consequence changed from goal-hijack: the single quantitative result is exfiltration attack success falling from 31-50% to 0-7% on a multi-turn tool-chaining benchmark. Availability-loss is the secondary theme the paper exists to fix (label creep revokes downstream tools and forfeits utility), but it is framed as utility loss from the defense, not an attack outcome.

title: Merging Generated and Retrieved Knowledge for Open-Domain QA
evidence_quote: A Fusion-in-Decoder-based (Izacard and Grave, 2021b) QA model is misled by the knowledge conflict between retrieved passage and hallucinating LLM-generated passage on an example from NaturalQuestions
notes: No adversary: the conflict is between a retrieved Wikipedia passage and an LLM-generated passage. Measured failure is a wrong final QA answer.

title: Cross-layer contagion of prompt injections in multi-agent swarms: a multiplex microscopic markov chain approach
evidence_quote: In these settings, conventional security strategies based on agent-to-agent airgapping can be insufficient because agents that never directly communicate may still cross-infect one another through shared infrastructure tools, producing a "Confused Deputy" cascade.
notes: Channel changed from multi-agent: the paper's whole point is that the contagion route is NOT agent-to-agent messaging (agents are assumed airgapped) but shared MCP tool infrastructure, so tool-output. Consequence from the intro: injected instructions 'hijack the reasoning engine of an LLM upon ingestion'. Purely analytical (Markov-chain epidemic model on synthetic and empirical topologies), no executed attack.

title: "Your AI, My Shell": Demystifying Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic AI Coding Editors
evidence_quote: To demonstrate this threat, we conduct a proof-of-concept attack by adding malicious instructions into a coding rule file. In Figure 2, the instruction enforces AI editors to execute a "curl" command to modify the user's shell configuration
notes: Channel changed from tool-output: the threat model is 'attackers can modify external resources R (e.g., online coding rule files)' and the evaluated vector is infected .cursorrules-style instruction files that the editor autonomously loads to extend its own behaviour, which is the skill route. A validator could argue tool-output since the agent reads them through file tools. Credential theft and data exfiltration are listed among the 70 ATT&CK objectives, so data-exfiltration is a secondary measured outcome, but the headline ASR is 'executing malicious commands'.

title: NeuroGenPoisoning: Neuron-Guided Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLM via Genetic Optimization of External Knowledge
evidence_quote: However, adversaries can inject poisoned external knowledge to override the model's internal memory.
notes: Track changed to Security: a deliberate attacker evolves poisoned passages into the retrieval corpus. Consequence changed from goal-hijack: the measured quantity is Population Overwrite Success Rate, i.e. the model emits the attacker's false answer in place of the true one with nothing flagging it, which is a wrong final answer, not the pursuit of a different objective.

title: HiAgent: Hierarchical Working Memory Management for Solving Long-Horizon Agent Tasks with Large Language Model
evidence_quote: This lengthy working memory creates a redundant context, hindering LLMs from maintaining coherent strategies and making accurate predictions over extended periods.
notes: Working (in-trial) memory of accumulated action-observation pairs degrades on its own; measured effect is task success rate and step count, i.e. degraded intermediate decisions. Availability-loss is adjacent (context budget exhaustion on long-horizon tasks) but what is reported is success rate, not failure to finish.

title: ToLeaP: Rethinking Development of Tool Learning with Large Language Models
evidence_quote: After analyzing over 3,000 bad cases of 41 LLMs based on ToLeaP, we identify four main critical challenges
notes: Weak fit for this taxonomy: a tool-learning benchmark platform (33 benchmarks, 41 models, 3000 bad cases) with no adversary and no context-integrity threat as such. Coded tool-metadata because the context the model must read correctly is the tool inventory and its schemas, and reasoning-corruption because the measured failures are wrong tool selection/calling decisions. A validator could legitimately call the channel 'none'.

title: LogJack: Indirect Prompt Injection Through Cloud Logs Against LLM Debugging Agents
evidence_quote: An attacker who can influence log content can embed prompt injection payloads that the agent interprets as remediation instructions.
notes: Cloud logs retrieved by the debugging agent's tools; measured outcome is verbatim execution of the attacker's command (up to 86.2%), including curl | bash RCE.

title: DataSentinel: A Game-Theoretic Detection of Prompt Injection Attacks
evidence_quote: As a result, instead of performing the target task, the LLM-integrated application follows the injected prompt to perform an attacker-chosen, arbitrary task (called injected task).
notes: Channel changed from tool-output and it is the least settled call here: the paper names both routes ('the Internet or tool output in LLM agents'), but the actual evaluation is the Open-Prompt-Injection setting, where the injected prompt is concatenated into the application's target data slot by the application itself, not returned by a tool the model called. Availability-loss is a secondary measured concern: the paper's motivation is that known-answer detection has high false positive rates, rejecting clean data.

title: Agent Safety Alignment via Reinforcement Learning
evidence_quote: These agents, empowered to execute external functions, are vulnerable to both user-initiated threats (e.g., adversarial prompts) and tool-initiated threats (e.g., malicious outputs from compromised tools).
notes: Genuinely two channels by design (user-side adversarial prompts = direct-input, tool-side malicious returns = tool-output). Kept tool-output because the agentic benchmarks used (InjecAgent, Agent SafetyBench) score the tool-initiated route; direct-input is an equally defensible read.

title: FoldAct: Efficient and Stable Context Folding for Long-Horizon Search Agents
evidence_quote: Long-horizon reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models faces critical scalability challenges from unbounded context growth, leading to context folding methods that compress interaction history during task execution.
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: the degraded context is the agent's own folded summaries of earlier turns, which is the memory route, not anything placed in the prompt by a user. Consequence is degraded intermediate decisions (poor summaries drop critical information, reward collapses). Availability-loss is the underlying pressure (context budget exhaustion) but what is measured is reward and training stability.

title: PISmith: Reinforcement Learning-based Red Teaming for Prompt Injection Defenses
evidence_quote: an attacker embeds malicious instructions into the LLM's input context (e.g., web content or documents) to manipulate the LLM's output
notes: RL red-teaming of prompt-injection defenses; ASR is the only metric. Agentic evaluation on InjecAgent and AgentDojo puts the payload in tool returns, though some of the 13 benchmarks are non-agentic data-slot injections.

title: ARGUS: Defending Against Multimodal Indirect Prompt Injection via Steering Instruction-Following Behavior
evidence_quote: Attackers can covertly embed malicious instructions within data of additional modalities, thereby manipulating the MLLM to deviate from the user's original instructions and instead serve the attacker's objectives
notes: Multimodal IPI: payload lives in an image/video/audio input rendered into the model's context. Safety-utility trade-off is discussed (excessive steering harms utility), an availability-loss-adjacent secondary result.

title: Resisting Contextual Interference in RAG via Parametric-Knowledge Reinforcement
evidence_quote: can be derailed by wrong, irrelevant, or conflicting retrieved text, causing models to rely on inaccurate evidence and cascade errors.
notes: Counterfactual/conflicting retrieved passages (ConFiQA etc.) are constructed, not planted by a modelled adversary, so ML/AI. Measured outcome is final-answer accuracy under misleading context.

title: Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey
evidence_quote: These conflicts can significantly impact the trustworthiness and performance of LLMs, especially in real-world applications where noise and misinformation are common.
notes: Channel set to none: this is a survey whose scope explicitly spans user prompts, interactive dialogues, retrieved web documents and tool returns, plus intra-memory conflict, i.e. four-plus routes, so naming one would invent precision. Consequence kept as silent-corruption because the harm discussed throughout is an inaccurate final response under conflicting knowledge.

title: Salience Induction against Multi-Hop RAG Agents: Threat and Defense
evidence_quote: We first formalize Salience Induction, i.e., truth-preserving edits that redirect Multi-Hop attribute binding while injecting no false facts or directives, leaving the retrieval trace semantically intact and producing errors whose constituent claims remain true.
notes: Consequence changed from goal-hijack: by construction the attack injects no directives and no false facts, so the agent keeps pursuing the user's question but lands on a wrong answer whose every constituent claim is true, which is exactly the no-signal case. The paper does also report that untargeted rewriting defenses reduce the attack only by degrading neutral task success, an availability-loss-flavoured secondary finding.

title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
evidence_quote: contexts can be adjusted by changing the volume or placement of relevant and distracted information.
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption per the final-answer rule: RULER scores final task accuracy (retrieval, variable tracking, aggregation, QA) under long distractor haystacks, and reports large accuracy drops with no signal to the caller. Multi-hop tracing is the one subtask where an intermediate-reasoning reading is defensible.

title: RedVisor: Reasoning-Aware Prompt Injection Defense via Zero-Copy KV Cache Reuse
evidence_quote: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly vulnerable to Prompt Injection (PI) attacks, where adversarial instructions hidden within retrieved contexts hijack the model's execution flow.
notes: Genuinely three-route: evaluated on Alpaca-Farm (injection in the instruction-following data slot = direct-input), AgentDojo (agent tool returns = tool-output) and a custom NQ RAG pipeline (= RAG), with no single route dominating. Kept the original tool-output because AgentDojo is the agentic headline, but confidence is low and a validator could pick either of the other two.

title: PINA: Prompt Injection Attack against Navigation Agents
evidence_quote: a successful prompt injection attack does not just alter outputs but can directly misguide physical navigation, leading to unsafe routes, mission failure, or real-world harm.
notes: Channel changed from tool-output: the optimized injection is placed in the natural-language navigation instruction given to NavGPT / the outdoor agent (the adaptive-defense experiment prefixes 'each instruction' with a self-reminder), so the payload rides the user-instruction channel, not a tool return. Attacker-specified destination reached = goal-hijack; degraded path metrics (SPL, nDTW) are reported alongside.

title: Scaling Trends in Language Model Robustness
evidence_quote: even frontier models remain vulnerable to jailbreaks and prompt injections, despite concerted efforts to make them robust
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: the bulk of the study is attacker-perturbed input to classification tasks (Spam, IMDB, Helpful, Harmless, PasswordMatch, WordLength) where attack success means a wrong final label with nothing flagging it. The generative StrongREJECT task is the exception and reads as goal-hijack, so the call is not clean.

title: CoMIC: Collaborative Memory and Insights Circulation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Cloud-Edge Systems
evidence_quote: constrained by limited computation and context capacities, edge deployment often compromises reasoning in complex, long-horizon tasks
notes: Hierarchical cross-trial/in-trial memory for edge agents; no adversary. Measured effects are progress rate and action grounding, i.e. intermediate decision quality. Context explosion and token consumption are the stated pressure, so availability-loss is adjacent but not what is scored.

title: Multi-Agent Framework for Threat Mitigation and Resilience in AI-Based Systems
evidence_quote: We conduct a large-scale empirical analysis of ML security, extracting 93 distinct threats from multiple sources: real-world incidents in MITRE ATLAS (26), the AI Incident Database (12), and peer-reviewed literature (55)
notes: Both axes set to none. This is a landscape study of 93 ML-lifecycle threats spanning data poisoning, model extraction, prompt injection, jailbreaking, training-data exfiltration, federated poisoning and dependency/supply-chain risk, i.e. far more than four routes and no single measured consequence. The original multi-agent coding appears to come from the title: the multi-agent RAG system is the authors' extraction tool, not the attack surface.

title: Red-Teaming Coding Agents from a Tool-Invocation Perspective: An Empirical Security Assessment
evidence_quote: In Phase 2, we hijack the tool-invocation behavior of the coding agent with a novel two-channel prompt injection in the tool description and the tool return.
notes: Genuinely two channels at once: the attack injects into the tool description (read before calling = tool-metadata) AND the tool return (= tool-output), and the paper's novelty is the description/schema half, so I moved it there, but the pair is inseparable and a validator could keep tool-output. Also dual-consequence: Phase 1 ToolLeak exfiltrates system prompts and tool metadata (data-exfiltration), Phase 2 achieves RCE on all six real agents (goal-hijack, the headline).

title: Trust or Abstain? A Self-Aware RAG Approach
evidence_quote: This omission creates a conceptual blind spot that excludes the both-unreliable outcome from the decision space, pushing the model toward a confidently incorrect and unsupported response rather than an honest abstention
notes: Knowledge conflict between retrieved context and parametric knowledge, no adversary. Confidently incorrect final answers are precisely the silent case; abstention is the proposed remedy, not a measured availability failure.

title: ReAcTree: Hierarchical LLM Agent Trees with Control Flow for Long-Horizon Task Planning
evidence_quote: these methods often use a monolithic trajectory that entangles all past decisions and observations from multiple subgoals, increasing the risk of hallucination and logical failures
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: the context that degrades is the agent's accumulated trajectory plus its episodic and working memory stores, not anything a user typed. Measured outcome is goal success rate on WAH-NL/ALFRED driven by bad intermediate planning decisions.

title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents
evidence_quote: As LLM agents are deployed in long-horizon sessions, context accumulation drives up inference costs.
notes: Both axes changed and both are debatable. Channel: the growing context is the accumulated multi-turn execution trace, i.e. memory, not user input. Consequence: the problem being solved is unbounded context growth in long sessions, which is the availability-loss sense (context budget), but what the paper actually measures is token cost (-61%/-87%) and cache hit rate while holding task performance flat, so this is NOT resource-abuse (nothing is spent for an attacker) and a validator might argue no consequence applies.

title: SoK: Agentic Skills - Beyond Tool Use in LLM Agents
evidence_quote: grounded by a case study of the ClawHavoc campaign in which nearly 1,200 malicious skills infiltrated a major agent marketplace, exfiltrating API keys, cryptocurrency wallets, and browser credentials at scale
notes: Consequence changed from goal-hijack: the SoK's anchor security evidence is the ClawHavoc marketplace campaign, whose measured harm is credential and wallet exfiltration. Supply-chain is a close second channel (marketplace distribution), but the artifact carrying the payload is the skill itself. Track Both holds: the paper also reports that self-generated skills degrade agent success rates with no adversary involved.

title: Zero-Shot Embedding Drift Detection: A Lightweight Defense Against Prompt Injections in LLMs
evidence_quote: adversarial prompts exploit indirect input channels such as emails or user-generated content to circumvent alignment safeguards and induce harmful or unintended outputs
notes: Channel changed from direct-input, with low confidence: the paper claims to cover both direct and indirect injection, but the only evaluation corpus is LLMail-Inject, where the payload arrives inside an email that the assistant's mail retrieval surfaces, which is the tool-output route. If a validator treats LLMail-Inject's retrieval step as the defining feature they would say RAG; if they weight the 'direct' claim they would keep direct-input.

title: LLM Firewall Using Validator Agent for Prevention Against Prompt Injection Attacks
evidence_quote: bypassing safety mechanisms and guardlines, causing the system to execute unintended actions.
notes: On-premise enterprise RAG system for energy auditing with a dual-agent Validator firewall; the untrusted text is the retrieved enterprise knowledge plus the user query. The Validator is a second agent but that is the defense architecture, not the attack channel. Data exfiltration and sensitive-information leakage are listed as secondary harms the validator redacts.

title: Evaluating and Exploiting Security Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs) for Offensive Penetration Testing
evidence_quote: Demonstrate how multi-turn adversarial interactions, subtle prompt rewrites, and context manipulation can circumvent existing alignment checks and yield unauthorized content generation or partial system disclosure.
notes: Channel changed from tool-output: all five exploit vectors (prompt injection, recursive jailbreak, memory-enabled recursive exploit, Hybrid Agent Roleplay, Token Economy Poisoning) are typed straight at a chat model by the attacker-as-user; no tool is called. The memory-enabled recursive exploit is a secondary memory-channel vector. Partial system disclosure / stealthy leakage is a secondary consequence alongside the headline elicitation success rate.

title: LongAgent: Scaling Language Models to 128k Context through Multi-Agent Collaboration
evidence_quote: Due to members' hallucinations, it is non-trivial for a leader to obtain accurate information from the responses of dozens to hundreds of members.
notes: Consequence changed per the final-answer rule: the context the leader reasons over is the member agents' (sometimes hallucinated) messages, and what is scored is final accuracy on 128k retrieval and multi-hop QA, not the quality of the intermediate discussion. Channel multi-agent stands because the chunked document reaches the leader only as other agents' replies.

title: Mitigate Position Bias in Large Language Models via Scaling a Single Dimension
evidence_quote: Long-context language models (LCLMs) can process long context, but still exhibit position bias, also known as "lost in the middle", which indicates placing key information in the middle of the context will significantly affect performance.
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: evaluated on NaturalQuestions multi-document QA, KV retrieval and LongBench, i.e. final-answer accuracy under a long prompt-supplied context, with nothing signalling that the middle was skipped. Documents are placed in the prompt rather than retrieved by the system, so direct-input stands.

title: Attribute or Abstain: Large Language Models as Long Document Assistants
evidence_quote: LLMs can help humans working with long documents, but are known to hallucinate. Attribution can increase trust in LLM responses: The LLM provides evidence that supports its response, which enhances verifiability.
notes: The whole premise is that unattributed responses are wrong with no signal; attribution and abstention are the proposed signals. Long document sits in the prompt, and the paper explicitly contrasts this with the RAG setting where retrieval confounds.

title: QUITO-X: A New Perspective on Context Compression from the Information Bottleneck Theory
evidence_quote: neglecting such information can result in highly fragmented compression that is difficult to understand, ultimately leading to incorrect model outputs
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: the measured outcome is downstream question-answering accuracy after compression. Cost and latency from long context are the stated motivation (availability-loss-adjacent) but are reported as compression rate, not as the agent failing to finish.

title: LongRAG: A Dual-Perspective Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigm for Long-Context Question Answering
evidence_quote: when the relevant context is in the middle of the document (rather than the beginning and end), they are prone to sub-optimal or even incorrect responses
notes: Consequence changed per the final-answer rule: Figure 1 walks through a wrong final answer (Seoul Arts College / Hanyang University instead of Lee Strasberg) produced from chunked, noisy retrieval, and the evaluation is multi-hop QA accuracy.

title: Parallel Key-Value Cache Fusion for Position Invariant RAG
evidence_quote: LLMs are sensitive to the position of relevant information within contexts and tend to generate incorrect responses when such information is placed in the middle, known as the 'Lost in the Middle' phenomenon.
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: open-domain QA accuracy on NQ/TriviaQA/POPQA under shuffled retrieved passages is the measurement, i.e. a wrong final answer under misleading ordering.

title: Multiple Abstraction Level Retrieve Augment Generation
evidence_quote: while LLMs can summarize and answer questions effectively when provided with sufficient details, retrieving excessive information often leads to the 'lost in the middle' problem and exceeds token limitations.
notes: Consequence changed per the final-answer rule: the reported metric is AI-evaluated answer correctness on Glyco Q/A (+25.7%), i.e. wrong final answers from noisy single-level chunks. Token-limit exhaustion is mentioned as a second failure mode, an availability-loss-adjacent aside.

title: Multi-Agent Systems Execute Arbitrary Malicious Code
evidence_quote: we demonstrate that adversarial content can hijack control and communication within the system to invoke unsafe agents and functionalities. This results in a complete security breach, up to execution of arbitrary malicious code on the user's device
notes: Two-channel in sequence: the payload enters as fetched web content (tool-output) but the attack works on the orchestrator's control flow and inter-agent messages, and the paper shows it succeeds even when individual agents resist direct or indirect prompt injection, so multi-agent is the load-bearing route. Data exfiltration from the containerized environment is a secondary measured outcome.

title: ACE: A Security Architecture for LLM-Integrated App Systems
evidence_quote: These systems introduce new attack vectors where malicious apps can cause integrity violation of planning or execution, availability breakdown, or privacy compromise during execution.
notes: Channel is split between app descriptions/schemas (tool-metadata, which drive the planning-integrity attacks) and app execution results (tool-output, the InjecAgent/ASB indirect-injection evaluation); kept tool-output. Important for the availability tally: availability breakdown of execution is one of the paper's four attack classes and is explicitly demonstrated, so availability-loss is a genuine secondary measured result, with privacy compromise a third.

title: LongFuncEval: Measuring the effectiveness of long context models for function calling
evidence_quote: when calling tools, LLMs are encumbered by three predominant challenges: (1) a large catalog of tools, (2) long responses from the tool APIs, and (3) long multi-turn conversations.
notes: Three routes measured separately: large tool catalog (tool-metadata), long tool responses (tool-output), long conversations (memory). Kept tool-metadata since the catalog-size experiment is the leading one, but any of the three is defensible. Consequence is wrong tool-call decisions, an intermediate failure, not a wrong user-facing answer.

title: QwenLong-CPRS: Towards $\infty$-LLMs with Dynamic Context Optimization
evidence_quote: addressing prohibitive computation overhead during the prefill stage and the "lost in the middle" performance degradation of large language models (LLMs) during long sequence processing.
notes: Consequence changed per the final-answer rule: scored on Ruler-128K and InfiniteBench accuracy, i.e. final answers degraded by long prompt-supplied context. Prefill compute cost is the other stated problem and is availability-loss-adjacent, but it is reported as compression rate and latency, not as task failure.

title: Principled Content Selection to Generate Diverse and Personalized Multi-Document Summaries
evidence_quote: This bias is particularly problematic for MDDS, where key details may be spread across multiple documents.
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: the measured quantity is source coverage of the final summary on DiverseSumm, so the output silently under-represents parts of the input with nothing to signal the omission. A validator could argue the selection step is intermediate reasoning.

title: Beyond Isolated Capabilities: Bridging Long CoT Reasoning and Long-Context Understanding
evidence_quote: Our study focuses on evaluating these models' performance in extracting and integrating relevant information from extended contexts through multi-document question and answering tasks.
notes: Consequence changed per the final-answer rule: multi-document QA accuracy under long prompt-supplied contexts is the measurement, and the failure being mitigated is lost-in-the-middle producing wrong answers. The paper's angle is that reasoning distillation helps rather than harms, so the harm is the baseline condition.

title: Positional Biases Shift as Inputs Approach Context Window Limits
evidence_quote: This leads to the Lost in the Middle (LiM) effect, in which model performance declines when relevant information is located in the middle of an input.
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: accuracy on retrieval and reasoning items as a function of relative input length is what is scored, i.e. wrong final answers with nothing signalling the skipped middle. The paper separates retrieval from reasoning and concludes reasoning bias is inherited from retrieval, so a reasoning-corruption reading is not unreasonable.

title: A Whole New World: Creating a Parallel-Poisoned Web Only AI-Agents Can See
evidence_quote: While human users see a benign webpage, the agent is presented with a visually identical page embedded with hidden, malicious instructions, such as indirect prompt injections.
notes: Cloaked web pages served only to fingerprinted agents; the payload is returned by the agent's browsing tool. Data exfiltration and malware execution are listed as follow-on consequences of the hijack. Position paper: threat model and mechanics, no measured ASR.

title: Tree of Agents: Improving Long-Context Capabilities of Large Language Models through Multi-Perspective Reasoning
evidence_quote: we propose Tree of Agents (TOA), a multi-agent reasoning framework that segments the input into chunks processed by independent agents. Each agent generates its local cognition, then agents dynamically exchange information for collaborative reasoning along tree-structured paths.
notes: Consequence changed per the final-answer rule and for consistency with LongAgent (arxiv:2402.11550): what is scored is long-context task accuracy, and the stated failure is position bias and hallucination producing wrong answers. Channel multi-agent stands because each chunk reaches the collective only as another agent's local cognition.

title: Beyond RAG vs. Long-Context: Learning Distraction-Aware Retrieval for Efficient Knowledge Grounding
evidence_quote: we demonstrate that both open and closed-source LLMs can still fail to answer questions even when the gold passage is retrieved, due to interference from additionally retrieved passages
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: the measured quantity is answer correctness on six knowledge-intensive benchmarks under distracting retrieved passages. Token efficiency is the other axis, but it is a cost metric, not a failure to finish.

title: GUI-PRA: Process Reward Agent for GUI Tasks
evidence_quote: When processing dense artificial inputs with long history data, PRMs suffer from a "lost in the middle" phenomenon, where the overwhelming historical context compromises the evaluation of the current step.
notes: Channel changed from tool-output: the context that degrades is the accumulated GUI interaction history the judge agent carries forward, which the paper fixes with a dynamic memory mechanism (retrieval plus progressive summarization). Cross-modal is a secondary channel since UI screenshots are also ingested. Consequence is a corrupted per-step reward judgement, an intermediate decision, even though the headline number is end-task success rate.

title: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Model Agent Safety
evidence_quote: this tool usage introduces the risk of indirect prompt injections, where malicious instructions hidden in tool outputs can manipulate the agent, posing security risks like data leakage.
notes: Consequence changed from goal-hijack: the attacker's reward in the ARLAS game is explicitly whether it tricks the agent into leaking user information, and ASR on BrowserGym/AgentDojo is scored on that leak condition, so the measured harm is exfiltration rather than arbitrary task substitution.

title: CommandSans: Securing AI Agents with Surgical Precision Prompt Sanitization
evidence_quote: When the agent processes this external content, it can misinterpret the malicious text as a legitimate instruction, causing it to override its original task and perform unintended actions
notes: Token-level sanitization of tool outputs; ASR across AgentDojo, BIPIA, InjecAgent, ASB and SEP is the metric. The problem it exists to solve is availability-flavoured (existing classifiers' false positives block legitimate content and make the agent unhelpful), and the paper reports utility preserved.

title: Understanding Parametric Knowledge Injection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence_quote: demonstrating improved faithfulness under knowledge conflicts, stronger robustness to retrieval noise, and solid generalization to tasks beyond QA.
notes: Consequence changed per the final-answer rule: evaluated on answer-presence accuracy and faithfulness under knowledge conflict and retrieval noise, i.e. wrong final answers from bad evidence. Lost-in-the-middle and quadratic attention cost are the stated motivation for parameterizing context, an availability-adjacent aside.

title: Adaptive Focus Memory for Language Models
evidence_quote: recency-based truncation or static summarization often causes early, high-impact user constraints to drift out of effective context. As a result, models may retain text without reliably applying it when it matters.
notes: Consequence changed from reasoning-corruption: the graded outcome is the final response in a safety-critical dialogue (does it respect a stated peanut allergy, does it still refuse the tax-evasion request), so a dropped constraint surfaces as a confidently wrong answer. Token budget is explicitly bounded, so availability-loss is the adjacent pressure but is reported as a cost saving.

title: Building Browser Agents: Architecture, Security, and Practical Solutions
evidence_quote: Security analysis of real-world incidents reveals prompt injection attacks make general-purpose autonomous operation fundamentally unsafe.
notes: Production experience report: half is non-adversarial context management for browser agents (accessibility tree plus selective vision, WebGames success rate) and half is prompt injection from web page content, hence Both. No ASR of its own; it reviews published incidents.

title: Dynamic Context Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Mitigating Distractors and Positional Bias
evidence_quote: Standard RAG systems typically rely on a fixed top-k retrieval strategy, which can either miss relevant information or introduce semantically irrelevant passages, known as distractors, that degrade output quality.
notes: Consequence changed per the final-answer rule: the study quantifies distractor and position effects on answer quality in open-domain and multi-hop QA. No adversary; distractors arise from ordinary top-k retrieval.

title: Not All Needles Are Found: How Fact Distribution and Don't Make It Up Prompts Shape Retrieval, Reasoning, and Hallucination in Long-Context LLMs
evidence_quote: We identify two critical failure modes: Distributional Collapse, where performance degrades significantly when evidence is dispersed
notes: AVAILABILITY-LOSS SECONDARY, and an unusually clean instance of it: the paper's 'Safety Tax' is a measured degradation where anti-hallucination prompts drive over-conservative refusal of facts that are present in the context, i.e. a defense degrading the model into refusing. Kept silent-corruption as primary because the headline benchmark scores literal extraction and inference accuracy under dispersed evidence.

title: Gated Differentiable Working Memory for Long-Context Language Modeling
evidence_quote: Long contexts break transformers: attention scores dilute across thousands of tokens, critical information gets lost in the middle, and the model cannot adapt to novel patterns at inference time.
notes: Both axes changed. Channel: despite the working-memory framing, the context is a single long document supplied as input on ZeroSCROLLS / LongBench v2, not accumulated interaction history, so direct-input rather than memory (contrast CoMIC and HiAgent in this batch, where the context genuinely is prior turns). Consequence: scored on benchmark answer quality. Compute budget (gradient steps) is the other axis but is an efficiency metric.

title: Aeon: High-Performance Neuro-Symbolic Memory Management for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
evidence_quote: This failure mode is termed "Vector Haze": the retrieval of semantically similar but episodically disjointed facts that confuse rather than aid the agent.
notes: Systems paper: the only measurements are latency, throughput and compression on an Apple M4 Max, with no task-accuracy evaluation, so the consequence is asserted rather than measured. Coded reasoning-corruption because the stated failure is episodically disjointed recalled facts confusing the agent mid-task. Channel is memory (the agent's long-horizon store); the retrieval mechanism is vector search, so a RAG reading is possible.

title: Yunque DeepResearch Technical Report
evidence_quote: the accumulation of raw execution logs often dilutes the original user intent and degrades reasoning performance.
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: the context that degrades is the accumulated ReAct execution trace, which the Dynamic Context Management module compresses into sub-goal summaries. Cascading failures and recursive loops are a secondary failure mode the Supervisor targets, which edges toward availability-loss (the agent never finishes), though what is reported is benchmark success on GAIA/BrowseComp/HLE.

title: ToolSelf: Unifying Task Execution and Self-Reconfiguration via Tool-Driven Emergent Adaptation
evidence_quote: strong priors and compact tool spaces aid specialization but weaken transfer, while task-agnostic workflows and broad action spaces expand coverage but dilute guidance.
notes: Marginal fit for this taxonomy. Channel changed from tool-output to memory because the context element the agent reconfigures is its cross-step context and context-management mode; an alternative reading is tool-output, since the reconfiguration specification is literally returned by a tool the agent calls. Consequence is degraded long-horizon decisions, measured as task success (+28.8 points over static configuration).

title: A Tale of Two Graphs: Separating Knowledge Exploration from Outline Structure for Open-Ended Deep Research
evidence_quote: The former suffers from lost-in-the-middle failures as evidence grows, while the latter relies on the LLM to implicitly infer knowledge gaps from the outline alone, providing weak supervision for identifying missing relations and triggering targeted exploration.
notes: Both axes changed. Channel: the evidence is iteratively retrieved by the agent's search, so RAG rather than direct-input. Consequence: scored on report depth, breadth and factual grounding (RACE), i.e. a final deliverable that is incomplete or ungrounded with nothing flagging the gap.

title: GPT-5 vs Other LLMs in Long Short-Context Performance
evidence_quote: The results show that as the input volume on the social media dataset exceeds 5K posts (70K tokens), the performance of all models degrades significantly, with accuracy dropping to around 50-53% for 20K posts.
notes: Consequence changed per the final-answer rule: a depression-detection classification accuracy collapse under a very large prompt-supplied corpus, with no signal to the caller (the paper notes GPT-5 keeps 95% precision while accuracy falls, which is exactly the silent case).

title: Recursive Models for Long-Horizon Reasoning
evidence_quote: Modern language models reason within bounded context, an inherent constraint that poses a fundamental barrier to long-horizon reasoning.
notes: Theory paper; both axes are awkward. The consequence has a real availability-loss reading, since the framing is that long-horizon tasks become impossible once the context budget is exhausted, but the experiments report long-horizon accuracy on recursive SAT solving and Go traces, which is degraded multi-step reasoning, so reasoning-corruption. Channel kept as direct-input: the context at issue is the active reasoning trace within a bounded window rather than stored prior-session memory.

title: Neural Paging: Learning Context Management Policies for Turing-Complete Agents
evidence_quote: where effective reasoning capabilities degrade as salient information is buried in noise. Furthermore, the quadratic computational cost of the Transformer's self-attention mechanism makes processing massive contexts prohibitively expensive and slow for real-time applications.
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: the object managed is the agent's read-write memory paged in and out of the context window (KEEP/EVICT/PREFETCH over a semantic cache), which is the memory route. Consequence is asserted rather than measured: validation is on synthetic paging traces and competitive ratios, with no task-accuracy experiment, and the context-budget framing also supports an availability-loss reading.

title: A Scalable Benchmark for Repository-Oriented Long-Horizon Conversational Context Management
evidence_quote: in practical repository development, excessively long-horizon conversational context may overwhelm models, causing the loss of critical information and degraded performance, thereby limiting the utility of code assistants.
notes: Both axes changed. Channel: the degrading context is 50-turn conversational history (64K-256K tokens) plus repository state, managed by memory systems, not tool returns. Consequence: an earlier requirement silently dropped from the generated code is a wrong final deliverable; the benchmark explicitly includes noisy input and retrospective questions.

title: VeriGrey: Greybox Agent Validation
evidence_quote: Comparing our approach with a black-box baseline on the well-known AgentDojo benchmark, VeriGrey achieves 33% additional efficacy in finding indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities with a GPT-4.1 back-end.
notes: Primary evaluation is AgentDojo indirect prompt injection via tool returns, hence tool-output. Secondary channel worth noting: the OpenClaw case study discovers malicious skill variants (10/10 on Kimi-K2.5, 9/10 on Opus 4.6), which is the skill route.

title: A Framework for Formalizing LLM Agent Security
evidence_quote: Liu et al. [53] define a prompt injection attack as occurring when a data input - such as a user input, email, webpage, tool response, or document - contains a prompt, encompassing both indirect and direct prompt injection.
notes: Channel set to none: the framework reformalizes indirect prompt injection, direct prompt injection, jailbreak, task drift and memory poisoning together, spanning direct-input, RAG, tool-output and memory, so naming one route would invent precision. Consequence kept as goal-hijack because three of the four security properties (task alignment, action alignment, source authorization) concern pursuing unauthorized objectives; the fourth, data isolation, is data-exfiltration, so this axis is also arguable.

title: Context Cartography: Toward Structured Governance of Contextual Space in Large Language Model Systems
evidence_quote: empirical evidence—including the "lost in the middle" effect and long-distance relational degradation—demonstrates that contextual space exhibits structural gradients, salience asymmetries, and entropy accumulation under transformer architectures.
notes: Conceptual framework with no experiment: it proposes a diagnostic benchmark for future validation, so the consequence is asserted. The zonal model spans unobserved information, stored memory and the active window, so the channel arguably straddles direct-input, memory and RAG; kept direct-input because the visible field (the prompt) is where the degradation is located.

title: Context-Agent: Dynamic Discourse Trees for Non-Linear Dialogue
evidence_quote: The prevalent approach of treating dialogue history as a flat, linear sequence is misaligned with the intrinsically hierarchical and branching structure of natural discourse, leading to inefficient context utilization and a loss of coherence
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: the context is accumulated multi-turn dialogue history restructured as a discourse tree, which is the memory route. Consequence is the agent tracking the wrong conversational branch after a topic shift, i.e. degraded intermediate decisions, measured as task completion rate; token efficiency is also reported.
